table.title: Weights and Measures
table.caption_extra: The following are the old and new standard weights and measures of the Chinese Republic:—

parts.label: Weights — Market Standard
rows: 1 shih chin = ½ kung chin = 500 grammes = 13 liang and 4 chien (Kuping weight)

parts.label: Capacity — Market Standard
rows: 1 shih sheng = 1 kung sheng = 0.966 sheng (old standard)

parts.label: Length — Market Standard
rows: 1 shih ch'ih = ⅓ of kung ch'ih = 1.4 ch'ih (old standard)

parts.label: Area — Old Standard
rows: 1 mow = ⅙ English acre = 240 sq. pu

parts.label: Area — New Metric Standard
rows: 1 kung mow = 1 are = 1000 sq. kung ch'ih

parts.label: Length Measure — Market or Municipal System
Superficies or Land Area — Market System

transcriber_notes: Rows: 135 in 19 parts, as printed (p. 563 right column: Weights and Capacity—Old Standard; p. 565: remaining sections). No totals printed.
Leaf p0589 (p. 564) between the two pages is a Business Announcement (advertisement) and is skipped.

Section heads (Weights / Capacity / Length / Area; then Length Measure / Superficies or Land Area / Measure of Capacity / Weight) and sub-heads (OLD STANDARD, NEW METRIC STANDARD, MARKET STANDARD, MARKET SYSTEM, STANDARD SYSTEM, MARKET OR MUNICIPAL SYSTEM) are combined into part labels.
Where several equivalents are bracketed against one quantity they are joined with ' = ' in one cell.

Ditto marks (,,) in the Equivalent column of the last seven parts are expanded to the words they repeat (e.g. 'of a metre', 'market feet'); the second row of Weights — New Metric Standard is printed '10 ,, ,,' (i.e. 10 kung ssu) and kept as printed.
'2 pu = 11 feet and 9 inches (English)': '(English)' is printed hyphenated over two lines as '(Eng-' / '[lish)'.

Kept as printed, apparently misprints: Weights — Market Standard '10 shih chien = 1 shih liang = 3¼ grammes' (500 g / 16 would be 31¼); Weight — Market System '1 hao = 0.0000032 of a kilogramme' (series would give 0.000003125); Weights — Old Standard '200 chin = 1 ying = 1.333 avoirdupois ounces'.
Fractions read under magnification: '1⅓ lb.', '½ kung chin', '⅓ English mile', '⅓ of kung ch'ih', '⅙ English acre'.
